4547.body:
## Outcome

The owner, 2026-10-28: "we should call that type of sticky Workstream agent a Mode. It's the same as a Workstream, but the sticky prompt and restarting it are first class."

A **Mode** is a Workstream whose Door has a saved first prompt (today's Opening prompt, #4465). Restarting it is a first-class action: roundup restarts the Door's session and types the saved prompt once as its first message.

- Rail: three sections, in this order (the owner, 2026-10-28):
  1. `WORKSTREAMS`: Workstreams with no saved prompt.
  2. `MODES`: each Mode by name.
  3. `AGENTS`: Agents with no parent Workstream or Mode. The user can later move one to nest under a Workstream or a Mode (drag, plus a menu item and a key); moving re-parents the Agent.
- A section with no rows is hidden, heading included (the owner, 2026-10-28: an empty `WORKSTREAMS` heading "shouldn't" show). An empty Rail shows only its empty view, as #4644 sets it.
- Agents with no parent are first class: `AGENTS` is a full section, never an overflow of `WORKSTREAMS`. The one link between them is the move: a free Agent can later become a subagent under a Workstream or Mode.
- The Rail footer gains `+ Mode` with the Mode kind icon, between `+ Workstream` (left) and `+ Agent` (right), styled as #4531 sets them. Section headings carry no add control.
- Each section heading collapses and expands its section (click, Return/Space, and ←/→ on the focused heading). The App remembers each section's state per Project across restarts.
- A Mode row shows a Restart control (↻) and a menu; Restart also has a key and a native menu item.
- Creating a Mode asks for its name and its first prompt; the prompt can be edited later.
- A plain Workstream has no saved prompt and stays in `WORKSTREAMS`.

## Scope

- Spec: new scenarios for Mode create, edit, restart, the three Rail sections and moving a root Agent under a Workstream or Mode; `GLOSSARY.md` adds Mode and folds "Opening prompt" into it. Check that the user label "Mode" does not clash with Permission mode's App copy, and rename that copy if needed.
- Then `apps/desktop/src/rail/`, the Workstream settings field from #4465, contracts if a Mode flag or restart RPC is new (Contract recipe, rule 4).
- No Clear (#4542). Pre-release data: no migration.

If the work exceeds one run, split into child Issues (sections first), each blocked by the one before.

Builds after #4465, which adds the saved prompt and restart typing.

5214.body:
## Outcome
The owner can turn a running or exited Agent into a Workstream, or save it as a Mode, from the Agent's Rail menu, without losing its conversation.

Owner ask (2026-10-31): "we should be able to convert an regular agent to a workstream or a mode". Owner chose (AskUserQuestion): the Workstream keeps the chat.

## Requirements
- **Make a Workstream** on an Agent row: the Agent's conversation continues as the lead (Door) of a new Workstream in the same Rail place, keeping its name, Terminal history and conversation id. It can then start children like any Workstream. A running Agent restarts on the same conversation once (as `agent.resume` with mode does) to pick up the Door's Brief and tools; an exited one converts without starting.
- **Save as Mode…** on an Agent row: asks for a name, then saves the Agent's Brief, tools, extras and model as a Mode that new Agents and Workstreams can start in. The Agent itself is unchanged.
- Both actions appear only where the Daemon accepts them (see #5213's rule: menus offer only actions the Daemon carries out). Children of a Workstream and Doors do not offer Make a Workstream.
- Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms (Workstream, Door, Mode); add any missing term in the same PR.

## Observer
Behaviour tests: Make a Workstream turns an Agent node into a Workstream node with the same conversation id, and `agent.resume` on it succeeds; Save as Mode adds a Mode whose Brief, tools and model equal the Agent's. The design critic judges the menu.

4452.body:
## Outcome

A new Agent or Door session starts idle: the user's first prompt is theirs. roundup sends no user-input message to start a session. The owner, 2026-10-27: "why does the workstream agent and the other agent both start eagerly before the user takes their chance to say anything? that is annoying and feels limiting … the first prompt in a session is the most important thing the user has, we can't take it from the user just to pass meta data and clarify intent … we should use the claude code inbox to communicate the agent/workstream meta harness coordination and meta information like todos etc".

- Every roundup-to-Agent text that is not the user's own words (Todo text, goal, intent prompts, limits, coordination, notes) goes through the Claude inbox (GLOSSARY "Claude inbox"), never as typed input or a launch-argument prompt. Today both the Door and the Agent it spawns start working before the user types.
- Sticky Workstream: a Workstream can hold the user's own saved opening prompt (for example `/compose /intent you are my JIRA orchestrator …`). When the user clears and restarts that Workstream's session, roundup sends that saved prompt as the session's first user message, because the user wrote it. The owner chose "send it for me" over prefill. A Workstream with no saved prompt starts idle.
- Fix the class: audit the daemon, `crates/agents/src/claude_code/` and the App for every path that writes into an Agent's input or passes a launch prompt (spawn, Door start, clear, restart, rewind, Ask), and move each non-user text to the inbox in this PR.

Scenarios: A4452
Specification: [scenarios/agent-lifecycle.md](https://github.com/roundup-app/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/agent-lifecycle.md)
Key: idle-session-start
Priority: 1
Mode: specify

## Acceptance

- Spawning an Agent or starting a Door leaves its Terminal at an empty prompt with no turn running; the Todo and coordination text has reached its Claude inbox.
- Clearing a sticky Workstream sends exactly its saved opening prompt once, as the first user message; nothing else enters as user input.
- The audit's list of input-writing paths goes in the PR body.

3194.acceptedChoiceExcerpt:
The owner chose: a queue with a per-Project cap; a Workstream counts as running while any of its Agents is working.

## Outcome

From a Todo's owner menu the user picks **New Workstream…**, which makes a Workstream that owns the Todo (its Home and its first Agent's work). The user picks when it starts: now, when a slot frees, or after another Todo is done. A Project setting caps how many Workstreams run at once. A Workstream counts as running while any of its Agents is `working`; one whose Agents are idle, ended or waiting on the user does not. A queued Workstream starts when the count drops below the cap, in queue order, and the queue is visible.
